audits.title: Quality assurance and gastrointestinal endoscopy: an audit of 500 colonoscopic procedures.
audits.standard: 62 colonoscopy process and outcome quality indicators with standard limits
audits.setting: Endoscopy unit, Hôpitaux civils de Colmar

cycle1.result: Within standards: caecal intubation 92%, inadequate preparation 24%, inappropriate procedures 9.7%, morbidity 0.4%, satisfaction 95.8%; outside standards: withdrawal time under 6 minutes 78%, forceps polyp removal 31%, polyps not recovered 12%.

audits.other_findings: Patients unsatisfied with waiting time 19% and with explanations 10%; the unit changed some practices.
audits.citation: Denis B, Weiss AM, Peter A, Bottlaender J, Chiappa P. Quality assurance and gastrointestinal endoscopy: an audit of 500 colonoscopic procedures. Gastroenterol Clin Biol. 2004;28(12):1245-1255. doi:10.1016/s0399-8320(04)95218-9. PMID: 15671936.

audits.title: Effectiveness of a continuous quality improvement program on colonoscopy practice.
audits.standard: Colonoscopy completion rate of 90% or more
audits.setting: Open-access endoscopy unit, Valduce Hospital, Como (secondary care)

cycle1.result: Crude completion 84.6% (range 80.4% to 94%); four endoscopists below 90%; polyp detection 34% (range 14% to 42%).

audits.intervention: Changes to sedation practice, more sessions for lowest performers and other organisational changes, over 6-monthly audit cycles for 4 years.

cycle2.result: Crude completion rose to 93.1%; all endoscopists reached 90% or more completion and polyp detection over 20%.

audits.other_findings: Complication rates did not change significantly.
audits.citation: Imperiali G, Minoli G, Meucci GM, Spinzi G, Strocchi E, Terruzzi V, et al.. Effectiveness of a continuous quality improvement program on colonoscopy practice. Endoscopy. 2007;39(4):314-318. doi:10.1055/s-2006-945196. PMID: 17273959.

audits.title: Point-of-care, peer-comparator colonoscopy practice audit: The Canadian Association of Gastroenterology Quality Program--Endoscopy.
audits.standard: Colonoscopy quality indicators including caecal intubation over 90% and withdrawal time at least 6 min
audits.setting: Academic and community endoscopy units (Canadian Association of Gastroenterology Quality Program)

cycle1.result: Mean caecal intubation 94.9%; mean withdrawal time 8.8 min, but 41.9% of colonoscopists had mean withdrawal under 6 min; polypectomy in 37%.

audits.other_findings: Withdrawal under 6 min was associated with lower polyp removal (mean difference -11.3%, P=0.01).
audits.citation: Armstrong D, Hollingworth R, Macintosh D, Chen Y, Daniels S, Gittens S, et al.. Point-of-care, peer-comparator colonoscopy practice audit: The Canadian Association of Gastroenterology Quality Program--Endoscopy. Can J Gastroenterol. 2011;25(1):13-20. doi:10.1155/2011/320904. PMID: 21258663.

audits.title: The national colonoscopy audit: a nationwide assessment of the quality and safety of colonoscopy in the UK.
audits.standard: National colonoscopy standards (caecal intubation, polyp detection, retrieval, comfort)
audits.setting: National colonoscopy audit; 302 NHS units, 2681 colonoscopists

cycle1.result: Unadjusted caecal intubation rate 92.3% (adjusted 95.8%); polyp detection rate 32.1%; 92.3% of resected polyps retrieved; 90.2% acceptable comfort.

audits.other_findings: Eight perforations and 52 significant haemorrhages; improvement from CIR 76.9% in the study seven years earlier; performance above national standards.
audits.citation: Gavin DR, Valori RM, Anderson JT, Donnelly MT, Williams JG, Swarbrick ET. The national colonoscopy audit: a nationwide assessment of the quality and safety of colonoscopy in the UK. Gut. 2013;62(2):242-249. doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2011-301848. PMID: 22661458.

audits.title: Quality audit of colonoscopy reports amongst patients screened or surveilled for colorectal neoplasia.
audits.standard: National Colorectal Cancer Roundtable Quality Assurance Task Group colonoscopy reporting criteria

cycle1.result: Indication and consent always documented; previous colonoscopy date 14%; caecum reached 94.4% with landmarks 78.8% and photodocumentation 67.2%; no procedural times recorded; polyp size 65.8%, morphology 62.2%, removal method unrecorded 20.7%.

audits.other_findings: Adenomas noted in 24.8%; most procedural indicators (date, medications, prep quality) recorded in over 98%.
audits.citation: Beaulieu D, Barkun A, Martel M. Quality audit of colonoscopy reports amongst patients screened or surveilled for colorectal neoplasia. World J Gastroenterol. 2012;18(27):3551-3557. doi:10.3748/wjg.v18.i27.3551. PMID: 22826619.

audits.title: Colonoscopy practice in lagos, Nigeria: a report of an audit.

cycle1.result: Caecal intubation rate 81.2%; bowel preparation good in 81.4%; polyp detection 6.8%.

audits.other_findings: Indication unspecified in 46.8%; quality judged suboptimal.
audits.citation: Onyekwere CA, Odiagah JN, Ogunleye OO, Chibututu C, Lesi OA. Colonoscopy practice in lagos, Nigeria: a report of an audit. Diagn Ther Endosc. 2013;2013:798651. doi:10.1155/2013/798651. PMID: 23533321.

audits.title: Colonoscopy audit over 10 years--what can be learnt?
audits.standard: Colonoscopy key performance indicators (time to caecum, withdrawal time, adjusted caecal intubation rate, polyp detection rate)

cycle1.result: All KPIs improved significantly over the audit period (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Nurse-recorded KPI data discussed at regular meetings with feedback to endoscopists.
audits.other_findings: Continuous audit over 10 years rather than discrete cycles.
audits.citation: Fraser AG, Gamble GD, Rose TR, Dunn JP. Colonoscopy audit over 10 years--what can be learnt?. N Z Med J. 2013;126(1382):25-35. PMID: 24154767.

audits.title: Colonoscopy quality in community hospitals and nonhospital facilities in Korea.
audits.standard: Colonoscopy quality indicators: caecal intubation rate, withdrawal time (6 minutes), bowel preparation adequacy, polyp number
audits.setting: Community hospitals and nonhospital facilities (referrals to six tertiary centres)

cycle1.result: Caecal intubation 93.1%; median withdrawal time 8.3 minutes, with 31.3% withdrawn within 6 minutes.

audits.other_findings: Community hospitals had longer withdrawal times than nonhospital facilities (median 9.9 vs 7.5 minutes).
audits.citation: Lee JG, Han DS, Joo YE, Myung DS, Park DI, Kim SK, et al.. Colonoscopy quality in community hospitals and nonhospital facilities in Korea. Korean J Intern Med. 2021;36(Suppl 1):S35-S43. doi:10.3904/kjim.2019.117. PMID: 32388944.

audits.title: Improved detection of adenomas and sessile serrated polyps is maintained with continuous audit of colonoscopy.
audits.standard: Colonoscopy quality performance indicators (polyp and adenoma detection rate, withdrawal time)

cycle1.result: Polyp detection 40.7% in 2004; adenoma detection 25.8% and SSP detection 4.5% in 2012.

audits.intervention: Continuous audit of colonoscopy performance with histology data added from 2012.

cycle2.result: Polyp detection 62.2%, adenoma detection 28.3% and SSP detection 14.7% in 2019.

audits.other_findings: Removal of polyps >1 cm stayed constant (11%); most SSP improvement occurred in the first 2 years of the histology audit.
audits.citation: Fraser AG, Rose T, Wong P, Lane M, Frankish P. Improved detection of adenomas and sessile serrated polyps is maintained with continuous audit of colonoscopy. BMJ Open Gastroenterol. 2020;7(1):e000425. doi:10.1136/bmjgast-2020-000425. PMID: 32675086.

audits.title: Quality in colonoscopy: time to ensure national standards are implemented?
audits.standard: National colonoscopy KPIs including minimum 100 procedures per year and ADR >15%
audits.setting: Eight hospitals in North East England

cycle1.result: 118 endoscopists: mean ADR 16.6%, PDR 27.2%, caecal intubation rate 91.2%; mean 78.5 colonoscopies in 6 months.

audits.other_findings: Colonoscopists performing fewer than 100 procedures a year had significantly lower ADRs; PDR can be a marker of ADR.
audits.citation: Neilson LJ, Dew R, Hampton JS, Sharp L, Rees CJ. Quality in colonoscopy: time to ensure national standards are implemented?. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2023;14(5):392-398. doi:10.1136/flgastro-2022-102371. PMID: 37581182.

audits.title: The 'ins and outs' of colonoscopy at Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, South Africa: A practice audit of the outpatient endoscopy unit.
audits.standard: ASGE/ACG benchmarks: adequate bowel preparation ≥85%; caecal intubation ≥90% overall and ≥95% screening; withdrawal time ≥6 minutes; ADR ≥25%
audits.setting: Outpatient endoscopy unit, Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, Johannesburg

cycle1.result: Adequate bowel preparation 77.6%; caecal intubation 97.0% overall and 96.3% screening; median withdrawal time 5.7 minutes; PDR 27.6%, ADR 15.6%.

audits.other_findings: Withdrawal time ≥6 minutes was associated with higher PDR and ADR.
audits.citation: Bouter C, Barrow P, Bizos D, Bobat B, Devar J, Harran N, et al.. The 'ins and outs' of colonoscopy at Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, South Africa: A practice audit of the outpatient endoscopy unit. S Afr Med J. 2020;110(12):1186-1190. doi:10.7196/samj.2020.v110i12.14419. PMID: 33403963.
